lens: Whoop/Strava athletic performance analytics: call strain and recovery, trend rings, personal records
name: Strain & Form Console
one_liner: A Whoop-style performance console for sales reps: call Strain, Form and personal records on every screen, a live coach rail beside every call, and OpenAI models named wherever they do work.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed: Whoop/Strava logic mapped to sales. Call Strain (0 to 21) rates how hard a call was for the rep, from turns, objections faced and persona difficulty. Form (fitness minus fatigue, Strava-style) shows whether the rep is sharp for a hard persona. Trend rings track skills; PRs mark personal bests per persona. Changed: the Mobbin side-panel screens (Dialpad, Fireflies) and competitors (Hyperbound, Second Nature, Yoodli) show live coaching as a rail beside the call, so the live screen is a coach rail plus rings, not rings alone. Whoop and Strava pages were not fetched in this run; those patterns come from general product knowledge and are not cited. palette.use: Light page background; replaces the default slate canvas.
Cards and sheets in light mode.
Primary text and dark-mode surfaces' contrast; not the old #071827.
1px hairline borders; replaces card shadows at rest.
Dark canvas for live call, pre-call briefing and landing hero.
Positive Form, recovery and rubric rings that are on target (graphics only, never body text).
Call Strain and effort rings; text on light uses #C2410C for contrast.
Personal records: one gold pulse per new PR.
Live coach cues and the active-cue glow, dark surfaces only.
Objection alerts and the End call action.

design_language.typography: Geist for UI (400 body, 500 labels) and Geist Mono 500 with tabular-nums for scores, strain, timers and transcript timestamps. Display 40/48 on landing; body 16px on mobile. Loaded with next/font/google.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Cards 16px radius with 1px line borders and no shadow at rest; controls 12px; chips are pills. Rings use 10px strokes with round caps. Two elevation levels maximum. Live surfaces get one soft glow, on the active ring only.
design_language.motion: Rings fill over 900ms ease-out on mount and on change; strain bars 600ms. Coach cue slides in over 200ms from the rail and fades after 6s. A new PR gives one gold pulse on its ring, not confetti. Everything is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion, with numbers updating instantly.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.75 stroke, 20px in controls, custom ring glyphs for Strain, Form and PR. Model chips use a small monospace label, not vendor logos.
design_language.theme_modes: Light is the default for practice, library, debrief, progress and team. Night is the default for live call, briefing and landing hero. Respects prefers-color-scheme, with a manual toggle. Each mode is one CSS-variable block so screens never hard-code colours.

navigation_and_ia: Desktop top bar: Practice, Library, Progress, Team, Contribute, plus a Cmd/Ctrl+K palette that jumps to any persona or past session. Mobile: bottom tabs Practice, Library, Progress, More; tabs hide during a live call. Practice is a Today page: your Form ring, one recommended persona with its target strain, and your latest PR. Routes: /practice, /library, /library/[slug], /create (wizard), /call/[id] (briefing, then live), /debrief/[id], /progress, /team (manager role), /contribute. Sign-in, MFA and access-code gate move into a single sheet. The demo-mode banner becomes a slim strip under the top bar.

live_coaching_and_scoring: The coach runs server-side as its own channel. Each rep turn sends the transcript delta, the persona profile and the rubric to a coach model (default gpt-4.1-mini, structured JSON). It returns typed cues with priority, the next best question, objection flags, provisional rubric deltas and the talk-track step. The persona model never sees coach output, so advice cannot leak into the character. Live rings are provisional; the full grader runs on End and replaces them with quoted evidence. Target: a cue within 2.5s p95 after the rep stops talking. Strain is computed live from turns, objections faced and persona difficulty. Self-rated D: 6.5 if latency holds; 4 if cues routinely arrive after 4s.
persona_library_and_wizard: Library: 240+ personas stored as persona JSON files in the repo, one per file, validated by a shared zod schema (role, seniority, industry, difficulty 1 to 5 mapped to strain bands, objection types, temperament, opening line, voice, rubric template). Target 15 job families with 16+ personas each, including every sales job in the brief. Filters: family, industry, strain, objection, channel and voice/text. Wizard: four entry points (job description, product URL, CRM or ICP notes, real transcript). Transcripts are redacted for phone numbers, emails and names before any model call. Output: a schema-valid draft, a 30-second test call, then Save or Export as a PR-ready file. Self-rated E: 6.5 if 240 personas ship with the wizard; 4 if fewer than 100 ship.
signature_moments: Form ring: fitness minus fatigue, so a rep sees whether they are sharp for a hard persona before dialing.
Strain forecast on every persona card and briefing: a pre-call estimate of how hard the call will be.
Whisper cue rail: one cue at a time, typed (Ask, Objection, Pace, Step, Close), with the reason one tap away.
Elevation timeline of the live score, with coach markers, so a rep can see exactly where the call dipped.
Persona wizard streams a live persona card as it writes, then runs a 30-second test call.
openai_fund_angle: Every surface names the model doing the work: model chips for grading, the coach, the persona wizard and voice, where voice is switchable between the OpenAI Realtime API and ElevenLabs. The Under the hood panel on each debrief shows model, prompt version, tokens and cost, so reviewers and users can audit how a score was produced. The landing footer shows Built with Codex, linking to AGENTS.md, which explains how contributors use Codex on persona PRs. Contributor invitations: the Add a persona wizard exports a PR-ready file plus a copyable Codex task prompt; good first persona issues are counted live on the landing page; persona authors are credited on cards (opt-in). Maintainers use Codex for PR review on persona and schema PRs, the PR-review and maintainer-automation workflow the Codex for Open Source program supports.

inspirations.source: Alekseia Leinikov: shadcn/ui vs MUI vs Mantine
inspirations.borrowed: Base UI as shadcn default since July 2026, and the bundle-size and owned-code data behind the library choice (MUI 140.2 KB, shadcn on Base UI 144.3 KB gzip).

implementation.migration_path: 1) Tailwind v4 and shadcn init on the Base UI preset, with the new token block, on a feature branch. 2) Build primitives: Ring, StrainBar, Timeline, CoachCue, ModelChip. 3) Persona JSON schema and seed the 240 personas; ship library and wizard. 4) Server-side coach channel with structured output and provisional scoring. 5) Screens in order: live call, mobile live call, debrief, briefing, progress, library, wizard, landing, team. 6) Remove the three.js orb and old component classes last. Each step is its own PR with before and after screenshots.

risks: Coach latency: cues that arrive after about 3s feel stale on voice. Mitigate with streaming, a small model and a rubric-only fallback if the coach times out.
Gamification: Strain and PRs can reward volume over quality or create anxiety. Keep PRs private by default and show Form as a range, not a verdict.
Trust: live provisional scores that disagree with the final grade erode confidence. Label provisional clearly and show the delta on the debrief.
Owned shadcn code means contributors maintain copied components. Pin components.json and add a CI check for drift.
Tailwind 3 to 4 and the token rewrite touch every screen; migrate screen by screen behind a flag.
Persona quality and stereotyping across 15 job families and industries need a review rubric and a verified badge before merge.

Council self-scores (my estimates): A 8, B 7, C 8, D 6.5, E 6.5. F1 SaaS 6 (crowded: Second Nature, Hyperbound and Yoodli already sell live coaching; the open-source core and Form retention are the wedge). F2 selling to entities 6 (licensing to training firms and call centres). F3 not worth building 3 (worth building as an open-source flagship, but not a clear win).
